items.readable_text:
Content:
In this lesson, we'll extend our knowledge of the secant-secant angle theorem to secant-tangent angles.

Content:
Consider the following diagram.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/ae99afd44905f701762596016ef1b136]

Content:
The points [MATH: A, B,] and [MATH: C] lie on the circle, [MATH: \overleftrightarrow{CP}] is tangent to the circle at [MATH: C,] where [MATH: P] is the intersection of [MATH: \overleftrightarrow{AB}] and [MATH: \overleftrightarrow{CP}.] We're also given that

Content:
[MATH: m\overset{\frown}{AC} = 150^\circ, \qquad m\overset{\frown}{BC}=60^\circ.]

Content:
Similar to the case with secant-secant angles, the measure of the secant-tangent angle [MATH: \angle P] equals half the difference between the measures of the larger and smaller intercepted arcs:

Content:
[MATH: m\angle P = \dfrac{m\overset{\frown}{AC} - m\overset{\frown}{BC}}{2}]

Content:
Substituting the given measures, we get

Content:
[MATH: m∠P|= (mAC^(⌢) − mBC^(⌢))/(2); = (150^{∘} − 60^{∘})/(2); = 45^{∘}.]
